post_text:
CQRS promised scale.

It delivered a hidden failure. I champion architectural purity.

To handle peak load, we implemented CQRS. The Command side scaled beautifully, tripling our write throughput instantly.

Latency metrics plummeted 80%. The team cheered.

🎉 But a cold dread settled in. The success felt brittle.

I watched the consistency lag monitor: zero. Perfect.

I assumed that zero lag meant the read model was perfectly synchronized. I thought the consumer group was healthy and progressing.

It never occurred to me that zero lag could mean the consumer was silently stuck, failing to commit offsets due to a transient JVM spike. The consumer was technically running, but it was reprocessing the same batch endlessly.

The Query database missed four hours of critical inventory updates. 💀 We faced a painful manual recovery, forcing the entire inventory reporting system offline for six hours.

💸

The Moral 👇

The absence of a failure metric is not proof of success; it is often proof of architectural blindness.
lesson_extracted: A consistency monitor must track progress and throughput, not just backlog size.
